question: Who was the second person to land on the moon?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Buzz Aldrin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Buzz Aldrin was the second person to set foot on the moon, following Neil Armstrong, during the Apollo 11 mission.
 
• The Apollo 11 mission took place on July 20, 1969, marking the first time humans landed on the moon.
 
• Buzz Aldrin and Neil Armstrong spent approximately 2 hours and 15 minutes outside the Lunar Module on the moon's surface.
 
• Buzz Aldrin's real name is Edwin Eugene Aldrin Jr., and he was a part of NASA's third group of astronauts selected in 1963.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apollo 11 Mission**

 
 
• The Apollo 11 mission was the first mission where humans landed on the moon and safely returned to Earth.
 
• The mission was launched by NASA, the United States' National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
 
• The spacecraft consisted of the Command Module (Columbia) and the Lunar Module (Eagle).
 
• Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins were the astronauts on this mission. Collins remained in lunar orbit while Armstrong and Aldrin descended to the moon's surface.
 
 
 
• **Neil Armstrong**
 
 
• Neil Armstrong was an American astronaut and aeronautical engineer, and the first person to walk on the moon.
 
• He was the mission commander of Apollo 11, and his famous words upon stepping onto the lunar surface were, "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind."
 
 
 
• **NASA**
 
 
• The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is an independent agency of the U.S. federal government responsible for the civilian space program, as well as aeronautics and aerospace research.
 
• NASA was established in 1958 and has been responsible for many notable space missions, including the Apollo moon-landing missions, the Skylab space station, and the Space Shuttle program.
 
 
 
• **Space Race**
 
 
• The Space Race was a 20th-century competition between two Cold War rivals, the Soviet Union (USSR) and the United States (USA), to achieve superior spaceflight capability.
 
• It began with the Soviet Union's launch of Sputnik 1 in 1957 and concluded with the USA's Apollo 11 moon landing in 1969.
 
• The Space Race was a significant aspect of the larger geopolitical rivalry between the two superpowers and spurred rapid advancements in space technology and exploration.
